name: Guru Bannanje Sanjeeva Suvarna
traditionPractice: Master practitioner of Badagutittu Yakshagana, preserving traditional repertoire, choreography, and regional performance techniques.
bio: A celebrated master and guru of the traditional Northern style (Badagutittu) of Yakshagana. He heads the Yakshasanjeeva Yakshagana Kendra in Udupi, dedicated to training next-generation artists. Over his career, he has preserved rare regional choreography, including historical Devadasi steps. He was honored with the prestigious Parthi Subba Award by the Karnataka Yakshagana Academy and has traveled to over 30 countries to showcase and teach the art form.

name: Patla Sathish Shetty
traditionPractice: Lead Bhagavatha (playback singer and director) representing the Tenkutittu (Southern style) Yakshagana tradition.
bio: A highly acclaimed lead vocalist and director in the Southern style (Tenkutittu) Yakshagana tradition. He serves as the principal Bhagavatha for prominent regional temple troupes, including the Pavanje Mela, driving the narrative and emotional landscape of night-long ritual acts. He is also the founder of the Yakshadhruva Patla Foundation Trust, an organization established to support and provide welfare for aging and underprivileged folk artists.

name: Bannanje Babu Amin
traditionPractice: Oral historian and researcher specializing in Tulu folklore, Paddanas (oral epics), and Daivaradhane traditions.
bio: A lifelong scholar and definitive voice on the indigenous folklore (Janapada) and religious customs of Tulunadu. Born in 1944, he has written extensive foundational texts documenting local history, including Tulu Janapada Acharanegalu and Tulunada Garodigala Samskritika Adhayana, with a specific focus on the historical hero-twins Koti and Chennaya. He has been recognized with the Karnataka Tulu Sahitya Academy Award and guides folk preservation efforts with groups like Samskriti Sampada.

His life's work centers on the documentation of tribal oral lore, the recitation of sacred Paddanas, and leading community-level preservation initiatives to protect localized shrines and religious customs from commercial distortion.
